value.note: A real Recommended Operating Conditions table, unlike the AMS1117. Both edges are hard: below 2.5 V the part is out of its specified operating range, above 6.0 V it is beyond recommended conditions (absolute maximum is 6.5 V, see abs_max_vin). A 5 V USB input sits comfortably inside; a 12 V input does not.

source.ref: Recommended Operating Conditions, p.3 — VIN Supply Voltage min 2.5, max 6.0 V

value.note: Absolute maximum power supply voltage. Only 0.5 V above the recommended maximum of 6.0 V, so there is very little headroom — a nominal 5 V rail with significant overshoot is a real risk with this part.

source.ref: Absolute Maximum Ratings, p.3 — VCC Power Supply Voltage 6.5 V

value.note: IMPORTANT NEGATIVE FACT: the AP2112 family is available ONLY in fixed 1.2 V, 1.8 V, 2.5 V, 2.6 V and 3.3 V options — there is NO 5.0 V variant. 'AP2112K-5.0' does not exist. This is the exact part number a model previously invented, and asserting the real option list here makes that provably wrong instead of merely unlikely. Output accuracy is +/-1.5%.

source.ref: Description, p.1 — 'available with a fixed output voltage of 1.2V, 1.8V, 2.5V, 2.6V, or 3.3V'; Electrical Characteristics AP2112-3.3, p.8

value.note: 250 mV typical at IOUT = 600 mA, for the 3.3 V variant specifically. Dropout is strongly variant-dependent on this part: the AP2112-1.2 table (p.4) lists VDROP typ 1000 mV / max 1300 mV, because a 1.2 V output cannot pass much current at low headroom. Do NOT carry the 250 mV figure across to other AP2112 output voltages. This low dropout is why the AP2112K-3.3 works from a 3.6 V Li-ion input where an AMS1117 (1.3 V max dropout) would not.

source.ref: Features, p.1 — 'Low Dropout Voltage (3.3V): 250mV (Typ.) @IOUT = 600mA'; Electrical Characteristics AP2112-3.3, p.8

value.note: 600 mA MINIMUM guaranteed continuous load current (the datasheet states it as a minimum, not a typical), measured for the 3.3 V variant at VIN = 4.3 V with VOUT between 3.251 and 3.350 V. Foldback short-circuit protection limits to 50 mA. NOTE for regulator-adequacy checks: an ESP32 needs a supply of at least 500 mA (ESP32 datasheet Table 5-2 IVDD), so this part clears that requirement but with only ~20% margin.

source.ref: Features p.1 ('Output Current: 600mA (Min.)'); Electrical Characteristics AP2112-3.3 IOUT(MAX) row, p.8

value.note: 1.0 uF at the input, shown as CIN in the typical application circuit and used as the test condition for every electrical characteristics table. Dielectric guidance (Note 4, p.2): 'It is recommended to use X7R or X5R dielectric capacitor if 1.0 uF ceramic capacitor is selected as input/output capacitors' — so a 1 uF Y5V part is not equivalent. The part is stable with ceramic, tantalum or aluminium electrolytic.

source.ref: Typical Application Circuit and Note 4, p.2; Electrical Characteristics test conditions, p.4-8

required_bypass_cap.reason: The AP2112 has no reference-bypass or noise-reduction pin. Its five pins are VIN, GND, EN, NC and VOUT (Pin Descriptions, p.2), and its 50 uVRMS output-noise figure is achieved without an external bypass capacitor — unlike the MIC5219 (470 pF on BYP) and LP2985 (10 nF on BYPASS).

value.note: 1.0 uF at the output. The features list calls the part 'Stable with 1.0 uF Flexible Cap: Ceramic, Tantalum and Aluminum Electrolytic', and Note 4 recommends X7R or X5R if a ceramic is used. Contrast the AMS1117, which needs 22 uF solid tantalum for frequency compensation — a 20x difference driven by the compensation scheme, which is exactly why these values must never be shared between LDOs.
